inputs.original_text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. Calling it an effort to expose vulnerabilities doesn’t erase the harm: staging a stunt around voting can feed the very false fraud claims that are used to weaken public trust and justify restricting access. We need safeguards that protect people’s votes without turning election security into another excuse to burden voters—especially those already facing barriers to participation.
inputs.modified_text: A Wisconsin jury convicted Harry Wait of election fraud and identity theft after he requested ballots for Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. Whatever the claimed motive, using other people’s identities to stage an election-security stunt can undermine trust—and give cover to those who want to make voting harder. The answer is safeguards that protect voters without piling new barriers onto people who already face obstacles to participating.
